content.jointProblem: Determine the mechanism by which combined cold-store thermal cycling, condensation and belt vibration drives fatigue cracking at crossmember-to-stringer weld joints in mild-steel hollow-section conveyor frames, and test whether changes to welding procedure, filler material or joint design reduce crack initiation and growth under representative low-temperature cyclic loading.

rationale.text: Erić's group directly studies fatigue and fracture of welded structural steel under combined mechanical cyclic loading and low-temperature thermal excursions.

sources.quote: His research group focuses on fatigue and fracture mechanics of welded structural steel joints subjected to combined cyclic mechanical loading and low-temperature thermal excursions

rationale.text: The group has the low-temperature fatigue testing infrastructure needed to move the company's problem out of room-temperature workshop testing.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models built in Abaqus

rationale.text: He has experimental evidence that superimposed thermal cycling during mechanical fatigue changes crack initiation and growth in welded plates.

sources.quote: superimposed thermal cycling (between −30 °C and +20 °C at 0.5 cycles per hour) during mechanical fatigue loading alters crack initiation and growth behaviour in butt-welded S275JR plates

rationale.text: He has measured and modelled weld-toe residual-stress relaxation under cyclic loading, which is relevant to explaining why as-welded frames may pass at room temperature but crack in service.

sources.quote: Initial peak longitudinal residual stress averaged +287 MPa in the as-welded state. After 1000 cycles at 180 MPa, surface residual stresses had relaxed to +61 MPa

rationale.text: He has prior industry consultancy experience on fatigue assessment of welded crane runway girders for regional steel fabricators.

sources.quote: Erić has carried out two consultancy engagements for regional steel fabricators on fatigue assessment of crane runway girders

rationale.text: His prior project combined sub-zero fatigue testing, residual-stress measurement, digital image correlation and finite-element simulation, matching the kind of integrated failure investigation AutomVoj needs.

sources.quote: The work combined fatigue testing at controlled sub-zero temperatures, X-ray diffraction residual stress measurements, digital image correlation, and sequentially coupled FE simulations

constraints.text: Testing must represent the cold-store operating range, typically 2 °C to 6 °C, not only ambient workshop conditions.
The plan must supply low-temperature cyclic-load testing because AutomVoj cannot do it in-house.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.

constraints.text: The two failed sections in storage and the site photos/measurements should be examined as part of the failure investigation.

sources.quote: we still have two of the failed sections in storage
We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits

constraints.text: Specimens and test welds must match the company's mild-steel hollow-section MIG/MAG welded and painted frame construction.

sources.quote: Mild steel and stainless steel MIG/MAG welded frame fabrication
welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery

constraints.text: Extended low-temperature testing must be scheduled around shared climate-chamber and servo-hydraulic machine access.

sources.quote: Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: AutomVoj has no dedicated R&D department, so the collaboration needs a clear technical lead and work plan rather than assuming internal research capacity.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department; technical development happens informally through project work

risks: Transfer gap: Erić's low-temperature fatigue evidence includes tests at −40 °C and on structural steels such as S355/S460/S275, while AutomVoj's problem is mild-steel hollow-section conveyor frames at 2 °C to 6 °C; the 2 °C to 6 °C condensation regime must be tested, not assumed.

The company suspects a combined thermal-cycling, condensation and vibration mechanism, but the published thermal-cycling work cited here does not establish that condensation or wet cold-store conditions are reproduced.

The failure cannot currently be reproduced in the company's room-temperature workshop, so a first experiment may still miss the actual service mechanism if load, temperature and condensation histories are not representative.
Shared access to Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine could delay an extended test campaign.
AutomVoj's lack of a dedicated R&D department may slow specimen preparation, instrumentation, data collection and implementation of findings.
Erić's availability is unknown and must be confirmed before committing to a schedule.
questions: Can Erić confirm availability and scheduling capacity for an extended low-temperature cyclic test campaign on the shared climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine?
What service temperature, vibration/load and condensation histories can AutomVoj provide from cold-store sites, and can loggers be installed on operating conveyors?
Can the two failed sections be released for destructive metallurgical and fractographic examination, and what weld procedure, filler metal, joint geometry and paint system records exist for them?
What budget, timeline and decision criteria would AutomVoj use to judge whether a changed welding procedure, filler material or joint design is successful?
Would AutomVoj also consider an industrial PhD route if the work needed a longer programme, or is a focused joint project the preferred format?
